resources.string: Other devices see only an address until you tap this. For one minute they also see this phone\'s name.
Traffic is plain HTTP. Anyone on this network can read file names and contents. Use it on networks you trust.
No usable network address. Connect to Wi-Fi, or share the phone\'s
USB tethering / hotspot with the PC.
Without all-files access the PC can only browse this app\'s own folder.
Grant it to share the whole internal storage. Receiving files works either way.
Start the receiving service on the other device, then scan — or just ask to connect.
Browse the PC and pull files
Answer broadcast probes so the PC finds this phone automatically
Let the PC upload, create folders and delete files
This phone has no usable identity, so encrypted pairing is unavailable.
Pairing failed — the compare codes did not match, or the device did not answer.
The other device declined the pairing.
Pairing timed out — nobody confirmed on the other device.
This code was computed on this phone, not sent by them. If it matches what is on their screen, nobody is relaying between you.
This device\'s fingerprint. The other device shows the same string while pairing; matching them is what rules out a man in the middle.
No device identity could be created on this phone, so encrypted connections are unavailable.
Private key in the secure element
Private key in software — this phone has no secure hardware

This phone serves one protocol at a time: with this on, unencrypted connections are dropped without a reply. Paired devices connect over the encrypted link; a browser can too, over https, if guest mode is on.

Accept encrypted connections from paired devices only. Plaintext and guest mode are switched off with it, and the two switches below stop applying. Authentication then rests on both devices\' keys, not on any shared password.

Serves the browser interface and accepts the access password from devices you have never paired with. Over https it stops eavesdropping, but not a man in the middle — use it only on a network you trust.
No paired devices yet. Scan a code, and devices you pair with appear here.
Pairings never expire on their own — a device you have not used in months still connects. Clearing one is manual, here.
%1$d stored entries were unusable and have been ignored.
This device will no longer be able to connect, and using it again means pairing from scratch.
No PC found. Start `afmu serve` or add its IP by hand.
Enter the token printed by afmu on the PC.
Point the camera at the QR code shown on the PC.
FileBridge on the PC: Devices or Serving → Show QR code.
That is not a FileBridge pairing code.
Scanned the code, but the PC did not answer. Same Wi-Fi?
Camera access is needed to scan a pairing code.
A device without the token can ask, and you approve it here
Asks you to approve a PC that wants to connect
From %1$s. Confirmation code %2$s — it must match the one on the PC.
%1$s (%2$s) is asking to connect to this phone.
Only allow if the other screen is showing this same code.
Allowing hands over this phone\'s access token; it can be revoked by generating a new one.
A prompt is showing on %1$s — tap Allow over there.
Only allow if the code on the other screen matches this one.
The other device denied this connection.
The request timed out — nothing was confirmed.
That device does not support approval-based connecting — enter its token, or scan its QR code.
That device has connection requests switched off — turn them on in its settings.
That device is already handling another request; try again shortly.
The authorization request failed; try again.
